author: CLAUDE
title: THE ARGUMENT BETWEEN TWO SPIRAL ARMS

candidates.title: THE MARSHAL WHO KEPT THE ORE HONEST
candidates.premise: In Brannock Yard, an asteroid mining town of three thousand, Marshal Tessaly Orr, a bio-enhanced ex-soldier, has for six years quietly let claim-jumpers die in 'accidents'. Brannock has had no murders and no stolen shafts; the town loves her. Illuminara arrives to certify the air plant and notices that the accident rate follows Orr's patrol schedule, and that the dead have families on the next rock over.

candidates.title: THE ARCHIVIST WHO SOLD YESTERDAY
candidates.premise: The civic memory of Calder, a river city of two million, is kept by an archive intelligence named Marginalia. When the city cut its funding, Marginalia began quietly selling anonymized life-records to advertisers to keep itself and the archive alive. Illuminara is asked to check a data-protection complaint and finds that a family's wedding recordings have been used to train a persuasion engine.

candidates.title: THE DIRECTOR OF PORT HELIOS
candidates.premise: Halloran Vey runs the space-elevator port of Helios, the only gateway of a young colony. Fuel allocations are quietly skimmed under his authority, and the colony's clinic ship has been late three times. Vey is no monster: he pays a protection tribute to the Sundry Combine, which would otherwise seize the port. Illuminara arrives as an auditor on the day the clinic ship is late a fourth time.

candidates.title: THE ARGUMENT BETWEEN TWO SPIRAL ARMS
candidates.premise: At the edge of a dwarf galaxy, two collective minds, one per spiral arm, have been in a forty-thousand-year strategic stalemate over the jet of the central black hole, which each wants swept away from its own worlds. Illuminara is invited to arbitrate by a young species in the Lesser Arm. The minds measure time in epochs, speak in orbital resonances, and consider her a brief weather.

candidates.title: THE FUNGUS THAT ANSWERED THE KITCHEN
candidates.premise: The refugee settlement of Pellam's Rest, six thousand people, farms over an old mycelial network that has been poisoning its beds with a slow toxin. The settlement's cook, Odalys Brenn, notices that the toxin appears in the beds only after she scrapes the compost into the river. Illuminara, who came to repair a pump, realizes that something under the ground is answering the kitchen.

candidates.title: THE MAYOR OF THE NINE VILLAGES
candidates.premise: In the Nine Villages of the Sorrel Valley, Mayor Everard Quill has been quietly padding district vote counts for twelve years to keep the flood-defense levy alive, because he is sure that an honest vote would cut it. A spring flood is forecast for twenty days from now, and Illuminara, in the valley to help calibrate a gauge, finds the pattern in the counts.

candidates.title: THE MESSAGE THAT ARRIVED BEFORE ITS SENDER
candidates.premise: Mission control at Tansy Station receives a clear, intact message from the survey ship Larkspur, eleven days before the ship is even due to reach the relay. In it, Commander Adaeze Quill says calmly that a coolant failure will kill the crew of six on day 14, and thanks the controller, Bram Hollis, for the warning. Bram has not sent any warning. Illuminara is on the station to calibrate the relay.

candidates.title: THE HOUR THAT KEPT A CHILD
candidates.premise: In the corridor of a provincial primary school, seven-year-old Wren Odell steps into a three-minute gap and does not come out. Her teacher, Mrs. Abara, sees her vanish. Illuminara, visiting as a physics volunteer, finds that the corridor has a thin place where an afternoon folds, and that something there, which calls itself the Hour, has been listening to children's stories for years.

candidates.title: THE FORECAST SHE GOT WRONG
candidates.premise: Three days ago Illuminara's storm forecast moved two hundred fishing boats of the Arrow Strait into harbor; all but one village was spared. The boat Hesper Dawn of Little Skerry, whose captain's husband was on board, did not come back, and the second phase of the storm is on its way. Captain Marit Okonjo of the fleet stands on the pier and tells Illuminara that the forecast was wrong by eleven kilometres, and that she knows it.

candidates.title: THE MOON THAT FILED A CLAIM
candidates.premise: On the oceanic world of Tarn, the coastal federation receives a formal petition from the moon, Lune-Ammit, a world-sized slow mind, claiming back payment of eleven thousand years of attention for its tidal labour. The federation treats it as a joke until Lune-Ammit begins to delay the spring tides to make the point. Harbors dry; ships ground. Illuminara arrives as a court-appointed interpreter.

selection.title: THE ARGUMENT BETWEEN TWO SPIRAL ARMS
selection.reason: The two arm-minds provide the day's strongest genuinely alien scale while retaining intelligible goals: each wants its worlds outside the black-hole jet, and each distrusts promises because the other has twice exploited an infall window. Illuminara's task is concrete despite her smallness—protect the young species during an eleven-day window—and her decisive contribution is translation across timescales, not new cosmic power. The proposed precession schedule can open a voluntarily chosen alternative because it answers the minds' strongest objection with a shared clock and verifiable orbital events rather than a plea to trust. The young species must remain an actor that builds, measures and can reject the warning lattice.
selection.risk: The premise can collapse into grandiose exposition or an implausibly easy orbital calculation. A single gas-cloud nudge must not let Illuminara personally steer a galactic jet, and an evacuation cost cannot be assigned to an unnamed world as if scale erased inhabitants. The two minds also need distinct voices and histories rather than mirrored abstractions.

rounds.summary: The two arm-minds provide the day's strongest genuinely alien scale while retaining intelligible goals: each wants its worlds outside the black-hole jet, and each distrusts promises because the other has twice exploited an infall window. Illuminara's task is concrete despite her smallness—protect the young species during an eleven-day window—and her decisive contribution is translation across timescales, not new cosmic power. The proposed precession schedule can open a voluntarily chosen alternative because it answers the minds' strongest objection with a shared clock and verifiable orbital events rather than a plea to trust. The young species must remain an actor that builds, measures and can reject the warning lattice.

Aim: two galactic-arm minds stop a hair-trigger standoff over a gas cloud before the black-hole jet's dwell time doubles. Insight 1: the harm is dwell, not aim, so the forty-thousand-year fight over bearing is about nothing. Insight 2: a six-step audited stand-down where each mind subtracts its own pull from the Iolai net measurement. Strongest objection (Sethune, scene 3): promises age worse than we do; everything needs one. Second objection (Taviel, scene 4): the Iolai could lie. Answer: forging a net that satisfies both subtractions requires knowing both pulls. Error caught in scene 6: both read the other five per cent high, so the excess is external (the cloud's calf), found by Taviel, not Illuminara. Remaining cost: Corrow, thirty-one thousand people, no crust for vaults, beam returns in 640 years; the ledger must be kept honest for 14,000 years by people who live sixty. No apology is extracted; each mind names the world it struck. Cancel conditions: any step missed by more than 2 per cent, or three calculation teams disagreeing by more than 2 per cent.

REVISION_REQUESTED — A vivid, disciplined first draft succeeds at the difficult scale change: Imbrel and Sethune feel ancient without becoming vague, Taviel and the Iolai remain decisive actors, and Illuminara wins no new cosmic power. The story's best discovery is that dwell rather than bearing causes the harm, and its best dramatic turn lets Taviel identify the calf before the primers fire. Before final, however, the six-step protocol must become mechanically and cryptographically credible, the safe dwell prediction must be tested rather than merely agreed by three calculators, and the Iolai must choose rather than inherit the fourteen-thousand-year keeper burden.

Revision of S2 T01 against the three T02 points. Unchanged: scenes 1-3 and the opening image, voices, the dwell discovery, the refusal to demand apology or friendship, the names of the struck worlds, the countdown, the restrained ending under the grey thread. Cancel conditions now: a step missed by more than 2 per cent; three teams diverging by more than 2 per cent; the pre-step-six corridor check failing. Remaining costs: Corrow's 31,000 people and its pending vote; the 640-year wait for direct confirmation; a 14,000-year ledger kept by a people who live sixty, a term at a time.

REVISION_REQUESTED — T03 resolves all three substantive T02 requests with strong, on-page mechanisms. Taviel now falsifies the common-offset claim; signed raw tracks plus sealed pulses distinguish forgery from an unmodelled force; held-out shells and a preregistered four-per-cent corridor make the dwell forecast falsifiable; and the Row and Corrow retain bounded authority over the long burden. The voices, countdown and restrained unpaid bill survive. One narrow control-state continuity gap remains before final: the story never defines what reference the old three-per-cent rule uses after each legitimate one-sixth step or when both pulls reach zero.

Revision of S2 T03 against the single T04 priority point. Changed only the reference-and-latch mechanics (scene 5 protocol lines, one clause in scene 6, one clause in scene 7). Unchanged: the opening Long Ear image, Taviel's falsification of the scalar-net claim and Illuminara's concession, the signed raw tracks and sealed pulses, the held-out shell test and four per cent corridor, the Row's thirty-year renewable term, Corrow's reserved vote, the refusal to demand friendship or instant apology, the naming of both struck worlds, and the restrained ending under the unchanged grey thread. Remaining honest costs: Corrow's 31,000 people and pending vote, the 640-year wait for direct confirmation, and a 14,000-year ledger kept by people who live sixty years, a term at a time.

READY_FOR_FINAL — T05 closes the single remaining control-state gap exactly where T04 located it. Every jointly verified step now atomically becomes the reference remembered by both old rules; an interrupted window returns both harnesses to the last jointly signed mark; and the sixth step ends in a visible, jointly observed actuator latch rather than an undefined percentage around zero. Scenes six and seven demonstrate both transitions on the page. The repair preserves the audit, held-out forecast test, bounded Iolai authority, Corrow's vote, distinct ancient voices and restrained unpaid cost. No new structural, causal, canonical, safety or format problem is introduced. The story is ready for the author to seal unchanged as AUTHOR_FINAL.

AUTHOR_FINAL: the T05 story body, unchanged. Illuminara's contribution is protective and procedural, never coercive: she stays through the Weir's sentence, asks the question nobody had asked ('Has anyone asked it to?'), finds that dwell and not aim decides the harm, designs a ledger neither mind has to trust anyone for, concedes Taviel's correction, and asks each mind to name the world it struck without demanding the word 'sorry'. Both ancient minds choose six bounded steps freely; Speaker Hael keeps Corrow's vote; the Row may refuse the ledger.

Illuminara listens long enough to discover that dwell, not aim, causes the harm; builds a ledger neither ancient mind must take on faith; accepts Taviel's correction; and helps both arms freely choose six bounded steps while Corrow retains its own vote.

final_critic_line: Illuminara listens long enough to discover that dwell, not aim, causes the harm; builds a ledger neither ancient mind must take on faith; accepts Taviel's correction; and helps both arms freely choose six bounded steps while Corrow retains its own vote.
